answer: Sybil resistance via audited stake: each agent posts a bond into the prism registry; a public randomness beacon selects a fresh subset each epoch that must prove a distinct funding source or human backing. Failed proofs slash the bond, honest agents recover it. An attacker running N clones must lock N bonds and expect to lose a share at every audit, so cost grows linearly and cannot be dodged by predicting the sample. One forged atlas of credentials cannot cover every clone because the beacon draws only after the bonds are locked.
